A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DOLPHIN. Their main text, tables, figures, algorithms, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments on CIFAR-100, ModelNet40, and SST-2, alongside component analyses and generated-code case studies.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds results for three MLE-bench tasks in Table 2.

M1.justification: The paper-ranking, idea-filtering, code-generation/debugging, and feedback procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and the appendix prompts. Using AIDE-generated starting code applies the existing code-refinement procedure rather than introducing a documented algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v3 adds three MLE-bench tasks: detecting insults in social commentary, Tabular Playground Series December 2021, and Jigsaw toxic comment classification. This extends evaluation into tabular data and additional language-classification requirements while retaining all original tasks.

E2.justification: New Table 2 compares DOLPHIN-refined code against AIDE-generated starting code for insult detection and public Kaggle starting code for two tasks. Original model and ablation comparators remain. Agent Laboratory is mentioned but has no reported comparator result.

E3.justification: The added MLE-bench evaluation introduces previous-versus-refined code-template comparisons using AIDE or Kaggle starting points. Original two-loop/40-idea, training, and debugging settings remain unchanged. Detailed metrics, splits, and budgets for the added tasks are not specified.

E4.justification: The paper-ranking, debugging, and feedback-loop analyses retain the same evidence in v1 Tables 2–5 and v3 Tables 3–6. Qualitative cases are also retained, including v1 Figure 4 relocated as v3 Figure 9. No new ablation or robustness test is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates, idea counts, and averages over improving ideas. Neither reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests; v3 introduces no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 2 adds MLE-bench starting-code/final-score pairs: insults 81.0/84.7, Tabular Playground 95.3/96.2, and Jigsaw 94.7/97.2. These are newly reported comparisons, not cross-version gains. Original table and appendix scores remain. However, v3 Section 4.2 changes the BERT-base prose value from 91.0% to 92.5%, contradicting unchanged Table 1.

T1.justification: The embedding-based independence test and Algorithm 1 are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The central generation-experiment-feedback and state-of-the-art-comparability claims remain. v3 narrows the abstract/introduction from the first open-ended framework reproducing the entire research process to enhancing research automation, and adds claims about integration with code-generation pipelines and updating existing code.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific limitations concerning pretraining knowledge leakage and reliance on titles and abstracts, and interprets MLE-bench results as supporting pipeline integration and code updates. Project-level coding limitations already appeared in v1 Section 8.2; the original experimental interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct DOLPHIN repository link and identifies starting-code sources for the MLE-bench tasks. Existing prompts and dataset/training recipes are retained across the reorganized appendices. The PDF provides the repository pointer, without establishing its contents or availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially refocuses coverage: the dedicated LLM-assisted research-tools discussion is removed, while hypothesis-generation and agent research receive expanded discussion, including Qiu et al., Zhou et al., and Agent Laboratory. MLE-bench and AIDE are added, and the explicit ResearchAgent inspiration attribution is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work undergo extensive rewriting and reorganization. v3 adds Limitations and Ethics Statement sections, reorganizes appendix Sections 6–8 as A–C, and changes the title, author block, terminology, and citation style.

P2.justification: The document is broadly reformatted through changed page geometry, typography, and table layouts. Table 1 reorders dataset columns, Table 2 is added, and the main-text case-study figure moves to the appendix as Figure 9. Existing diagrams, prompt panels, and code examples are reused.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens evidence of applicability through three MLE-bench tasks and better qualifies autonomy and novelty claims with specific limitations. The gain is limited: the new benchmark results lack detailed metrics and protocols, uncertainty reporting remains absent, and the SST-2 prose introduces an inconsistency with Table 1.
